mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, thereby driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS levels, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate suggests a strong labor market, which may boost consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in at least 60% of the 20-day periods following UNRATE decreases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in both GDP and housing starts indicates strong economic growth and increased demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following simultaneous increases in GDPC1 and HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests increased economic activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in at least 70% of the 60-day periods following INDPRO increases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment suggests a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following PAYEMS increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales suggests strong consumer demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in at least 60% of the 5-day periods following RSAFS increases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in federal funds rate alongside a decrease in unemployment rate suggests a tightening monetary policy, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following simultaneous increases in FEDFUNDS and decreases in UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high and increasing CPI suggests inflationary pressures, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show negative returns in at least 50% of the 20-day periods following CPI increases, the hypothesis fails.
